clue.text: Launch fan club around A Turner

indicators.note: around tells us the fan-club word wraps itself about the next pieces

parts.note: a cult is a devoted following, a fan club
a tap is something you turn to let water run

explanation.surface: A supporters' group launches a campaign for the painter Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' with a capital looks like the painter J. M. W. Turner; here it is simply a thing you turn. 'around' wraps the fan club about A and that.
explanation.definitionFit: To catapult something is to fling or launch it forcefully.

clue.text: Strange relation from China?

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the following word are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd relative who seems to come from the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' asks for the letters of RELATION to be rearranged. The question mark marks the definition as an example: China is one Eastern country among many.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from China is Eastern, from the Orient, though the question mark shows China is just one instance.

clue.text: Some uplifting motett etc of group of musicians

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
some says only part of the following words is wanted, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Part of a rising motet and so on, from a band of singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks ETTETCO from 'motett etc of', and 'uplifting' turns it upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet (here in its French-style spelling) is an ensemble of eight players or singers.

clue.text: Beans for scientists workplace party

parts.note: a laboratory, LAB for short, is where scientists work
Lab is the abbreviation for the British Labour Party

explanation.surface: Beans being grown for a science lab's party.
explanation.walkthrough: LAB appears twice: once as the laboratory and once as Labour, the British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Lablab is a tropical climbing plant grown for its edible beans, the hyacinth bean.

clue.text: Dull chap among spies turns to form of exercise

indicators.note: turns says the whole assembled string is then read backwards
among says the dull fellow is placed in the middle of the spies

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of spies
a bore is a tedious person

explanation.surface: A tedious man in the secret service takes up a fitness routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' places the bore inside the spies, giving CIBOREA, and 'turns' reverses the lot. 'turns to' reads like 'takes up' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobic workouts are a style of exercise that raises the heart and breathing rate.

clue.text: Georgian city hosting Conservative lot

indicators.note: hosting means the city takes the next piece inside it as a guest

parts.note: Bath, a spa city in England, is famed for its Georgian architecture

explanation.surface: A city of Georgian terraces welcomes a Tory group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgian' points to the US state or the country of Georgia; it is BATH, the English city full of 18th-century Georgian buildings. 'hosting' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch, like a lot, is a set of things dealt with together.

clue.text: Fungus, a pungent plant left out

indicators.note: out says the named letter is dropped from the plant's name

parts.note: garlic is a strong-smelling plant

explanation.surface: A mushroom, a smelly herb, has been left out of the recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops the L (left) from the plant, leaving GARIC; 'left out' reads as one phrase in the surface but splits into abbreviation and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Agaric is the name for gilled mushrooms such as the fly agaric.

clue.text: Boy picking up first of vinyl records

indicators.note: picking up means the boy collects the next piece and holds it within his name

parts.note: Archie is a boy's name

indicators.note: first of takes only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A lad grabs the first of the vinyl records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' gives V from 'vinyl', and 'picking up' puts it inside ARCHIE. 'records' looks like the discs the boy collects; here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a collection of historical records or documents.

clue.text: This paper makes favourable impression

parts.note: in can mean in favour, popular, favoured
a die is a stamp that makes an impression in metal

explanation.surface: The newspaper is pleased that it creates a good impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This paper' is the Independent, where the puzzle appeared; INDIE is its nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Independent newspaper is called the Indie, and the clue appeared in it.

clue.text: A section of company with special skills

parts.note: dept is the short form of department, a section of a firm

explanation.surface: A part of the firm with expert abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adept is being highly skilled or proficient.

clue.text: Technique for attacking high caseload

indicators.note: high, like drunk, suggests the letters are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: A method of assault on a heavy workload.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' seems to belong to the attack (scaling walls); it is the anagram signal for CASELOAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Escalado is the old military method of scaling fortress walls with ladders to attack.

clue.text: Tenth hit — Humble Pie — you can play it here

indicators.note: pie is a printer's term for jumbled type, so the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tenth chart hit for the band Humble Pie, a song to play.
explanation.walkthrough: Humble Pie was a rock band, but 'Pie' is printers' jargon for a jumble of type and signals an anagram of TENTH, HIT and HUMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a children's party game in which a hidden object must be found.

clue.text: Go to Lithuania — you'll find ear bone there

indicators.note: you'll find tells the solver the answer is sitting inside the words before

explanation.surface: Travel to Lithuania to discover an ear bone.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'gO TO LITHuania'.
explanation.definitionFit: An otolith is a small calcium deposit in the inner ear that helps balance.

clue.text: Geeks put Greek character in river

indicators.note: in places the Greek letter within the river

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Nerds throw a Greek letter into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' might suggest a person from Greece; it is a letter of the alphabet. The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Techies are technology enthusiasts, computer nerds.

clue.text: What camper needs to show humour

parts.note: to be something is to show it as a quality
droll means amusing, full of dry humour

explanation.surface: Something a camper needs is a sense of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: To show humour is to BE DROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroll is the rolled-up sleeping bag and blanket a camper carries.

clue.text: Rector and priest always one to provide comfort

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel
ever means at all times, always

explanation.surface: The rector and a priest are always on hand to console.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI, the Old Testament priest, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A reliever eases pain or distress, bringing comfort.

clue.text: With a view to the future that school has AIM S in autumn

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'With a view to the future that school has AIM S in autumn (4-4)': 'AIM S' is garbled OCR and no source gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: With a view to the future that school has AIM S in autumn

clue.text: Falls over in a river once more

indicators.note: over says the whole string is turned upside down, read upward in this down entry

parts.note: again means once more

explanation.surface: Something falls into a river all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses A, R and AGAIN together, giving the falls on the US-Canada border.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the great waterfall system on the border of the US and Canada.

clue.text: Following directions, medic ordered adrenalin, good for a source of hormones

indicators.note: following means the medic comes after the directions

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north
doc is a doctor, a medic

indicators.note: ordered says the drug's letters, with the good, are rearranged

parts.note: the drug's name as printed, whose letters are the fodder; one of its two As is surplus to the answer, so the anagram uses ADRENLIN

explanation.surface: Following instructions, the doctor prescribed adrenalin, which is good for the glands.
explanation.walkthrough: E and N are compass points. 'ordered' rearranges ADRENALIN with G, but the answer has only one A, so the setter's fodder is one A over.
explanation.definitionFit: An endocrine gland, such as the thyroid, secretes hormones straight into the blood.

clue.text: Energy given your old Liberal radical

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned Liberal politician, full of energy, is a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radical' looks political beside Liberal; in chemistry a radical is a group of atoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethyl is a chemical radical, a group of two carbons and five hydrogens.

clue.text: Pester and grimace where marital harmony is rewarded

parts.note: to dun is to press a debtor repeatedly
mow is an old word for a grimace or pulled face

explanation.surface: Nagging and pulling faces in a household that is meant to be happy.
explanation.walkthrough: Great Dunmow in Essex holds the Dunmow Flitch, a side of bacon given to a married couple who have not quarrelled for a year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essex town awards a flitch of bacon to couples proving a year of contented marriage.

clue.text: Record length in sword

indicators.note: in puts the length inside the sword

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A record length for a fencing sword.
explanation.walkthrough: An LP, a long-playing record, spelt out as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: An LP is a long-playing vinyl disc, a record.

clue.text: Henry VIII was certainly not that rational

parts.note: the famously stout king was certainly not slim
Henry VIII was a king of England

explanation.surface: A remark that the Tudor monarch was certainly not reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII was notoriously fat, so he was certainly not a THIN KING. 'that' points at the definition 'rational' in the surface, but it refers to THIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking, as an adjective, describes someone who reasons, a rational being.

clue.text: Claim time to make folds

parts.note: a plea is a claim or appeal

explanation.surface: Asking for time to fold the laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: To pleat cloth is to press it into regular doubled creases.

clue.text: Divers bowels get the bends

indicators.note: divers is an old word for various, suggesting the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Scuba divers suffer gut pains when they get decompression sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like the underwater swimmers who get the bends; it means 'various' and signals an anagram of BOWELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbows are bends, as in pipe joints or a river's sharp turns.

clue.text: Does drug taken by former Newcastle manager

indicators.note: taken by means the drug goes inside the manager's name

parts.note: Glenn Roeder managed Newcastle United football club
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Does the ex-Newcastle boss take ecstasy?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb; it is the plural of doe, female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Female deer are called does, and roe deer are a small species of deer.
